newsitem.title: USA: Growing livestock sector behind China soy demand.
newsitem.headline: Growing livestock sector behind China soy demand.

text.p: Growing demand for livestock products helped fuel China's huge soybean and soybean product purchases this year, U.S. Agriculture Department General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait said.

"In China, there is a very rapidly growing market for livestock products and of course if you're going to produce more animals and you want to have good feeds for them you'regoing to have some soybean meal in the premixes and the feed rations," Goldthwait said in an interview on USDA Radio.
He also said China put more cropland into wheat this year.
USDA has pegged China 1996/97 soybean meal imports at 2.3 million tonnes, up from 929,000 tonnes the prior year and soybean imports at 1.9 million tonnes, up from 795,000 tonnes.
Demand for soybeans and soybean products has been driving prices higher.

"What we're seeing is demand for the beans domestically and internationally from a variety of sources that reflects what we're seeing all around which is increased demand for livestock products, for meats, which reflects the income growth that's being enjoyed really throughout the world," Goldthwait said.
He said Japan had bought "a little more" this year compared to last and that Western Hemisphere destinations, especially Mexico, had taken "considerably more" this season.
